significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that harmfulness judgments contain "two causally separable contributions" whose relative weighting predicts over-refusal and jailbreak behavior, with lexical processing shallow and semantic-intent processing deeper; this is principally a form-(iii) ordering and predictive coupling, strengthened by a form-(ii) causal decomposition. It establishes both a phenomenon—the two failures occupy opposite lexical/semantic regimes—and a mechanism that constrains two distinct behaviors at once, which would materially revise the interpretation of single-axis controls such as Arditi et al.'s 2024 refusal-direction ablation and steering. Verified false would informatively rule out this shared-pathology account and imply that over-refusal and lexical-obfuscation jailbreaks require distinct mechanisms; the true and false states are therefore determinate despite the hypothesis's narrower applicability to "many jailbreaks." Topic-substitution self-check: replacing the decomposition with only "improve LLM safety through interpretability" would not justify this score; the above-median value comes specifically from the claimed two-contributor ordering and its joint explanation of opposite failures.

reach.justification: The named handle is "Semantic-Recompute," a "training-free inference intervention" that reads and re-weights the lexical-trigger and semantic-intent components; it is ex ante because it changes the safety decision before the model completes the potentially harmful response. Although the directions require per-model calibration, the conclusion transfers as the predicted relation "high-lexical/low-semantic" for over-refusals versus "low-lexical/high-semantic" for successful jailbreaks, so re-extraction is meant to recover a specified quadrant structure rather than merely provide an open-ended search procedure. The hypothesis speaks broadly of "an aligned LLM" and hands deployers a gating-time control intended to reduce both refusal errors and attack success, giving it uptake beyond the mechanistic-interpretability researchers who identify the components, though it does not establish transfer outside instruction-tuned language models or across all jailbreak mechanisms. Topic-substitution self-check: generic mechanistic safety work would not earn this reach score; it is supported by the specifically named inference-time handle, its action window, and the cross-model relation asserted after recalibration.
